description:
Problem: an invalid attempt (reply fails validation or the dispute contract) is retried once on the same reviewer and then the run moves up the chain (selection.py RETRYABLE_ABSENCES, 2026-10-23 decision _project/decisions/oracle-small-reviewer-model-2026-10-23.md). When the failure comes from the process itself (2026-10-27: the concedes template bug on #3453), every reviewer fails the same way and escalation spends large, huge and max for nothing. When it comes from a weak model's formatting, escalation is right. A fixed rule cannot tell them apart.

Outcome (owner 2026-10-27: 'Use Jev to classify the error as retry (same model), stop (process blocked), or escalate (move up to the next tier)'): after each invalid attempt the loop asks Jev (TypeSafe jev-1.14.0, the JevSession used by classify.py) one choice question with criteria for retry, stop and escalate. Jev's state holds only the redacted validation message, the reply shape fingerprint (types and counts, never raw reply text), the reviewer tier and model role, the attempt number for that reviewer and the earlier invalid messages in this run. The answer, its probability and confidence are recorded on the attempt artifact, so artifact replay reproduces the choice. Selection: retry runs the same reviewer (at most MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_REVIEWER; a retry beyond it becomes escalate); escalate moves to the next reviewer; stop ends the run pending with the reason 'stopped: the process is blocked (<message>)', posting nothing that passes. Fallback when Jev is unavailable, unkeyed (local without a key), answers outside the three labels or below the 0.60 confidence bar: retry the same reviewer once, then stop; never escalate without a Jev answer. The review body shows the recovery next to each invalid attempt.

Decision gates:
1. Before coding, run the question on recorded cases (the #3453 attempt messages; Haiku/Luna format failures from the 2026-10-23 evidence if retrievable; a malformed-JSON case) and record Jev's answers; if Jev classifies the #3453 contract failure as escalate or the format failures as stop, stop and ask the owner before shipping.
2. Amend _project/decisions/oracle-small-reviewer-model-2026-10-23.md: the escalation mechanism becomes Jev-decided; record the owner instruction and date.

Item guardrails: no decision ever passes because of recovery; stop and every fallback fail closed to pending; Jev never sees raw reply text, diffs or secrets; the Jev call is bounded by its existing timeout and counts against no reviewer slot.
